title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Allowing the Procuratorate to Send Court Clerks to Accompany the Chief Procurator or Procurator in Court to Support Public Prosecution
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Allowing Procuratorates to Send Clerks to Appear in Court with Chief Procurators or Procurators to Support Public Prosecutions

Fa (Si) Tong [1986] No. 3

Hubei High People's Court:

We have recently received a letter forwarded by the Supreme People's Procuratorate from two comrades of the Criminal Procuratorial Department of Hubei Provincial People's Procuratorate and the Yuan'an County People's Procuratorate, reflecting that some courts have refused to allow procuratorates to send clerks to appear in court with chief procurators or procurators to handle recording work. Upon our study, we are of the opinion that although the Criminal Procedure Law, the Organic Law of the People's Courts, and the Organic Law of the People's Procuratorates do not expressly provide whether a procuratorate may send a clerk to appear in court with a chief procurator or procurator to support a public prosecution, in light of trial practice, it is beneficial to the work for a procuratorate to send a clerk to appear in court with a chief procurator or procurator, and such practice should be permitted.

This notice is hereby given.

November 7, 1986
